CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit to assess the management of generalized anxiety disorder, insomnia, persistent fatigue, and tension-type headaches, with particular attention to medication efficacy and symptom progression.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his scheduled follow-up appointment, having maintained a symptom diary as advised. He reports that his generalized anxiety disorder remains stable, with further reduction in anxiety levels noted over the past month. He attributes this to the continued effectiveness of sertraline at 300 mg daily and ongoing cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT). Mr. Smith expresses a sense of increased control over his anxiety, particularly in social settings.
Regarding his insomnia, Mr. Smith notes that while the frequency of nocturnal awakenings has decreased to two to three episodes per night, he still experiences significant difficulty in achieving restful sleep. He continues to take trazodone at 100 mg at bedtime, which he reports has been helpful, but he still feels unrested upon waking. He expresses a desire to explore alternative sleep aids or techniques to enhance sleep quality.
Mr. Smiths tension-type headaches remain stable, occurring approximately once or twice weekly, with a consistent intensity rating of 4 out of 10. He reports that ibuprofen 600 mg continues to provide adequate symptomatic relief. However, he is interested in discussing preventive strategies to further reduce the frequency of these headaches.
Persistent fatigue remains a significant concern for Mr. Smith, who continues to experience notable afternoon lethargy. He reports that while bupropion at 150 mg daily has helped stabilize his energy levels to some extent, he still encounters episodes of cognitive fog and diminished motivation, particularly during stressful work periods.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 300 mg daily (continued) 2. Trazodone 100 mg at bedtime (continued) 3. Lisinopril 10 mg daily (continued) 4. Ibuprofen 600 mg as needed for headache relief (continued) 5. Topiramate 150 mg daily (continued) 6. Lorazepam 1 mg twice daily as needed (continued) 7. Melatonin 20 mg at bedtime (continued) 8. Modafinil 100 mg in the morning (continued) 9. Bupropion 150 mg daily (continued)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to engage in physical activities, including yoga and brisk walking, which he finds beneficial for managing stress. He reports a commitment to mindfulness practices, although he acknowledges that work demands occasionally disrupt this routine. He maintains an active social life, which he finds instrumental in alleviating anxiety symptoms.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Anxiety levels stable; improved sleep quality; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms reported. - Neurological: Headache frequency stable; intensity rated as mild to moderate; no dizziness or visual disturbances noted. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Persistent fatigue continues; no fever or significant weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 120/75 mmHg, HR 70 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.7F - General: Alert, oriented; appears mildly fatigued but engaged; mood appears stable with mild anxiety. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed; no tenderness in the temporal region. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears stable with mild anxiety.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 300 mg daily. Maintain CBT sessions; reassess progress at the next visit. Lorazepam at 1 mg twice daily as needed for acute anxiety will remain on the regimen. 2. Insomnia: Continue trazodone at 100 mg at bedtime. Consider adding a sleep hygiene regimen and explore the potential for a trial of a low-dose trazodone taper if sleep quality does not improve in the next month. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Continue topiramate at 150 mg daily; maintain ibuprofen at 600 mg as needed. Discuss potential referral to a neurologist for evaluation of preventive therapies if headache frequency or intensity does not improve. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Continue bupropion at 150 mg daily; encourage ongoing exercise and stress management techniques. Re-evaluate fatigue levels at the next appointment and consider adjusting the bupropion dosage or exploring additional agents if no improvement is observed.
Follow-up appointment is scheduled for 2029-10-01 to continue monitoring symptom progression, medication efficacy, and address any new concerns. Mr. Smith is encouraged to maintain a detailed log of his symptoms, medication responses, and any potential triggers for his anxiety or headaches to facilitate ongoing management.
